_doc: AUTHORED reading of Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35 for the background behind Prairie Avenue: Indiana Avenue's east frontage, 20th to 22nd Street, and the two lots of East Twenty-first Street behind its 2101-2105 corner (T-3009, piece 2 of T-2983, which tools/census_prairie_1904_background.py ranks: every Indiana lot of the 20th-21st block is seen from the avenue's walks). The T-1842 census (chicago/prairie_1904_v1/data/sheet_census/sheet-35.json) counts Prairie frontages only, and edges_census_s35.json holds T-2982's named lots on 20th Street and Calumet, so these rows are read here, in the same frontage contract, for tools/trace_prairie_1904_footprints.py (sheet '35w') and tools/draft_prairie_1904.py. Four fronts carry 1911 commercial uses whose 1904 state nothing in hand attests (2001-2003, 2101-2105 and 2129-2131 Indiana, 215-217 E. 21st): they are read and traced but ruled phase_unresolved and not drafted (T-3013). The fifth, 2133 on the 22nd Street corner, is not read here at all: the sheet draws it as a five-storey brick block, 68 ft, lettered BRANCH P.O., with a saloon on the corner, stores along 22nd Street (202-212 E. 22nd ride on its lot) and a two-storey frame dwelling at its east end, and those stores and rear buildings want their own reading beside its 1904 state (T-3013). 213-217 E. 20th, inside this block's north-east corner, are T-2982's and are not here.

reading.by: Read by eye from the committed sheet 35 scan (1602 x 2000 px) at 3x over the Indiana lots, the 1904 grid's parcel lines drawn over each crop, 2026-10-22.
reading.conventions: Sanborn colour: pink brick, yellow frame, blue stone. A crossed square marks a stable. D = dwelling. Storey figures as printed (B = basement).
reading.limits: A 1911 label is a 1911 observation (study ruling 11): the garages, the printing works, the repair shop and the post office are not carried back to 1904. The scan is coarse (0.186 m/px), so a storey figure on a small outbuilding is not always legible and is left unread. Robinson 1886 plate 10 ends north of 20th Street, so no earlier plan checks these outlines. No dimension is claimed beyond the trace.

polygons.reading_1911: 3-storey brick building, 40 ft, across both lots from Indiana Avenue to the alley, lettered PRINTING and POWER ELEV., with an office on the first floor

frontages.why: A 1911 printing works with nothing in hand to say what stood here on 1 July 1904: no named record, no 1904 directory row in the T-1837 study and no earlier plan south of 20th Street. Its 1911 use is not carried back (study ruling 11), and building a house in its place would be invention, so its 1904 phase is left open and the draft stands nothing here until T-3013 reads it.

frontages.why: The church fills the lot from Indiana Avenue nearly to the alley. No 1904 source for it is in hand, so its presence is inferred: a masonry church of this size, with a 90 ft spire, is not a building put up and lettered in the seven years to 1911 without a trace in the study, and the sheet is the only plan. The draft stands it as a site record (draft_prairie_1904.json `sites`), its dwelling and stable from the trace.
